tg.conclusion: Reviewed Telegram v0.117.0 to v0.123.0 with the exact published command contract. New: `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` (logs out on Telegram's side, then forgets the profile's app id and hash, proxy password, bots' history sessions and cli-core state; a same-named bot's token stays; agents cannot start it over MCP), `models set|add`, `store import` for synthetic test stores, `schedule pause|resume` and repeatable `--at`, `muted:` in search and stats, `contracts/wirecat.json` listing the HTTP hosts. `messages sync --all` now leaves out muted chats (counted in `limited.muted`; `--with-muted` or `history_muted true` reads them), EmbeddingGemma is the default text model (219 MB, no `--accept-terms`, e5-small kept where it is the only model), an agent's `contacts link` proposes and needs `--reason`, `search messages --timeout 30s` may run about 29 seconds, `--offline` refusals answer `offline.refused` exit 5, `contacts context|prepare` read only the profile's own scope, е matches ё, BotFather's chat is kept out of search, tg's HTTP reaches only declared hosts, `serve` exits on an outdated build, and the store moves to version 63 (cli-core 0.630.0). New settings `history_muted` and `keep_store_runs_for_days`. RU/ES changelog, commands, cli-contract, configuration-reference, mcp, sessions and topic-search reviewed. Native erratum left for tg-cli: archive.md still says `messages sync --all` reads every chat. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.92.0 and none of its planned items (chat notes, emoji reaction rankings, remaining max parity, location messages) shipped.

max.conclusion: Reviewed MAX v0.103.0 to v0.111.0 with the exact published command contract. New: `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` (ends the MAX session, then erases the token, profile files and the shared layer's data for the profile; the bot token stays; refused while `max serve` runs), `store import` (synthetic data into a test store), `schedule pause|resume`, repeatable `--at`, `participants_count` and `muted:` in search and stats, part of a name in `from:`/`chat:` (`from:Name*`), part of a word in message text (`*word*`, three letters minimum, matched as written apart from case and ё/е), and `sync.progress` events in the run record. Changed: `contacts unlink` requires `--from person:<uid>|person:me`; `--offline` on a command that needs MAX answers `permission_error` (`offline.refused`, exit 5); `contacts context|prepare` read only accounts of the profile's sphere and return `accounts`; `list:` in message search is refused (`query.unsupported-field`); remote embeddings over plain `http://` are refused off this computer (`model.address-refused`); `search messages --timeout` can run up to 29 seconds; test-data people are hidden from people lists; a damaged store answers `configuration_error` (`store.damaged`) and blocks writes; the store moves to version 66 (cli-core 0.642.0, cli-base 0.96.0). Fixed: `messages sync --all` reports progress inside a chat, daily and one-time schedules wait out `rate_limited` up to six hours, `max serve` exits with code 3 when outdated so systemd starts the new version, and setting the clock back no longer blocks sync. Topic search now defaults to `embeddinggemma` (`--accept-terms` is a no-op). RU commands copy and EN/ES bot, changelog, cli-contract, commands, mcp, people, sessions, topic-search, troubleshooting and usage reviewed (pinned source links moved to v0.111.0). Native gaps left for max-cli: query-language.md does not describe the new search syntax (`*part*`, `from:Name*`, `muted:`, `list:` refused), the changelog does not name the topic-search model change, and empty-default option rows still print a pair of backticks. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.76.0; none of its planned items shipped.

zm.conclusion: Reviewed Zoom v0.67.0 to v0.71.0 with the exact published command contract. New: `zm app` prints the Zoom app checklist (`--json`), `session end` deletes the saved login and keeps meetings, `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` (refused while an archive schedule runs; does not revoke at Zoom), `meetings sync --rescan`, and `meetings sync` stops before `--timeout` and resumes (`stopped`, `remaining`). `meetings export` works read-only and over MCP without `--output`. `session start --json --answer-stdin` asks for `client_id`, and a sign-in with no app fails with `zoom.client-id-missing`. `search all` drops `--max-meetings`: it reads the profile's meetings through the search index, ranked with other sources, at most 3 hits per meeting, with `cue_ref` on transcript hits, and never builds the index. An agent's `meetings link` becomes a proposal (cli-core 0.619.0), while the owner's `--yes` applies at once. `--offline` refusals use `offline.refused` exit 5, and the store moves to schema 57. RU/ES changelog, commands, search and zoom-app reviewed. docs/sessions.md still says there is no logout command, so a reviewed portal correction names `session end` and `account remove` in EN/RU/ES; the search.md `zm_write` correction stays. The authored Meetings guide (EN/RU/ES) was checked against v0.71.0 commands, flags and fields and needed no change, so its pin moves to v0.71.0. The roadmap is unchanged: audio recording of attended calls, notes/speaker naming, broader preparation and additional platforms remain planned; none shipped.

drive.conclusion: Reviewed drive 0.62.0 to 0.65.0 from the changelog and the docs diff since v0.61.0. Added: `drive documents add <url> --profiles <a,b|all>` keeps one Drive document's text in the shared store as a source added by hand, for memo's Add to memory. It tries the named profiles in order, at most `max_add_profiles` (default 5, at most 50), moves on only after an access refusal, answers `duplicate_of` for a file a sync already imported, and does not run over MCP. Also added: `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data`, `folders browse [--parent]`, and `schedule pause|resume`. May break callers: a profile with no saved sign-in fails with `oauth.missing`, not `oauth.expired`. `memories add --supersedes` retires the old memory only once the owner confirms. The shared store moves to version 57 and then, on cli-core 0.634.0, to 64. Fixed: a document's owner and last editor no longer land in your memory or its review, and a spent Google quota is a rate limit, not a permission refusal. RU/ES changelog (kept in English, as before), commands, configuration and usage reviewed. Since `documents add` ships, the memo troubleshooting correction that worked around it was retired. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.61.0: its Next item, `mirrors watch` as a background service, has not shipped.

memo.conclusion: Reviewed memo 0.145.0 to 0.149.0 from the changelog and the docs diff since v0.144.0. Added in these versions: `memo digest history` and a digest's scheduled run that catches up on syncs first (0.145.0), the `task-triage` agent that proposes tasks from chats and meetings (0.146.0), a morning digest that reaches Telegram whole (0.147.0), `memo people delete`, `memo records clear` for a test import and sending records from n8n over the remote MCP server (0.148.0), and `memo organizations delete` (0.149.0). RU/ES business, people, remote and tasks updated, commands and changelog follow the English reference, changelog sections kept in English, as before. memo 0.149.0's people page now links agent_merges to the config file itself, so the site's correction for `memo config set` is dropped and RU/ES carry that wording. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.131.87.

wa.conclusion: Reviewed WhatsApp v0.30.0 to v0.38.0 from the changelog and the source diff. wa now asks WhatsApp at most 20 times a minute per profile, 10 at once (was 60 and 20), and `messages sync <chat>` asks the phone for a page every 5 to 10 seconds; `--pause` of `messages download --all`, `attachments download` and `store gaps repair` defaults to 5s. `session start` waits for the phone's own signal that its history sync is done (five minutes of quiet at most), `session start phone --json --answer-stdin` lets a window such as WireCat Desktop link by pairing code, the QR event carries `expires_at`, and `--json` reports the pairing code and the history wait as events. `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` unlinks a profile and forgets it. `contacts add` and `contacts rename` save a WhatsApp contact name (remove and import stay refused); `contacts unlink` needs `--from`, `contacts context` reads only the asked account's scope. Queries gain name patterns in `from:` and `chat:`, `*part*` inside words, `participants_count` and `muted:`; `store import` loads a synthetic test store; `serve` exits when its build is out of date; `--offline` on a networked command is refused with `offline.refused`. From cli-core the reference also gains `models set`, `models add` (`--accept-terms` no longer needed), embeddinggemma as the default model, `search all --only meetings` without `--max-meetings`, `contacts link --reason`, bot `--button` and `--no-buttons`, `messages sync --with-muted` with `history_muted`, `keep_store_runs_for_days`, `owner_languages` and the `crm.*` settings. RU/ES changelog (0.31.0 to 0.38.0), commands (English body, as before), archive, attachments, configuration-reference, limits, people, query-language, sessions and usage reviewed; the RU query-language `kind` row's wrong wording was corrected. No correction changed. Upstream errata left for whatsapp-cli: sessions and archive still say `session start` stops after 45 seconds of quiet, and the changelog does not say that `messages sync --all` now leaves muted chats out. The roadmap is unchanged and none of its planned items shipped.

gcal.conclusion: Reviewed gcal 0.35.0 from its changelog and the docs diff since v0.34.0. May break callers: the MCP Registry entry no longer starts `mcp serve --profiles all`; `--profiles` is a required argument, so a client set up from the registry asks which profiles to serve. A client set up from the old entry keeps `--profiles all` until it is set up again. The overview (#189) is rewritten as a sales page: what you get, the ideas a newcomer would not guess (including that over MCP a delete does not ask), an example, why gcal against its comparison, a start and plain limits. RU/ES index retranslated and changelog updated and accepted. The roadmap did not change.

mail.conclusion: Reviewed mail 0.29.0 to 0.32.0 from the changelog and the command diff since v0.28.0. 0.29.0: `rules apply` runs up to 15 minutes by default in a terminal and 45 seconds over MCP, reads headers newest first and saves batch by batch; a run that reaches its limit answers `state: partial` with a cursor, and `rules apply --cursor` goes on from there; `rules apply` takes `--yes` over MCP; `score:` and `--kind` judge a sender from the store; the time-limit error names the time limit. 0.30.0 builds on cli-core 0.659.0 and mends a shared config with a small slip, keeping a `.bak` copy. 0.31.0: `rules import --format gmail` takes its own `--yes` over MCP, `rules export` answers over MCP, a resumed `rules apply` that read nothing points to `MAIL_TIMEOUT` over MCP or adds `--timeout 30m` in a terminal, and `messages delete --rules` keeps mail from senders the owner wrote to. 0.32.0: a `readonly` level no longer stops `mail sync`; `deny` still does. RU/ES changelog and commands reviewed. The Email guide and the Yandex Telemost page were checked against the new behaviour: neither says `rules apply` needs a long `--timeout`, fails on a big mailbox or that `readonly` stops sync, so both stay unchanged; the pin moves to v0.32.0. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.17.0: its Next item, a live test of Gmail over OAuth, is not claimed as done. Earlier: Reviewed mail 0.25.0 to 0.28.0 from the changelog and the command diff since v0.24.0. `rules add --do meeting-notes:<provider>` keeps the matched mail whole and protected and saves it as a meeting on sync; `rules apply --yes` saves notes stored before the rule, and its dry run counts them. Telemost notes in Yandex's older layout take the text before the first heading as their summary, and the footer is not stored. `doctor reports show|create`, the `crm.<provider>:<account>.activities` setting, the local-only model switch, declared hosts, and sync on a fresh install with an unreadable shared config. RU/ES changelog and commands reviewed. The Email guide does not describe any of these and stays correct; its pin moves to v0.28.0. The new Yandex Telemost page documents the meeting-notes rule. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.17.0: its Next item, a live test of Gmail over OAuth, is not claimed as done.

b24.conclusion: Reviewed b24 0.26.0 and 0.27.0 from their changelogs and the docs diff since v0.25.0. Added: client files (`files list`, `files download`, `files sync`), whose text `search all` finds as the `crm_file` hit kind, and `files: deny` that `api call` cannot get round. May break callers: `api call` hides more signed links, Drive's not-found is `not_found` (exit 6), `account remove --delete-data` is cli-core's shared command with new refusal codes, and an MCP server no longer offers `schedule exec`. Fixed: a deal moved in the same second its stage-task rules were set opens its task. The roadmap moves client files and documents from Next to what works today; the other Next items have not shipped. RU/ES of the changed pages updated and accepted.

pbx.conclusion: Reviewed pbx 0.8.0 from its changelog and the docs diff since v0.7.2. May break callers: `meetings transcribe` answers the report the other phone CLIs give (`audio_ms` instead of `audio_seconds`, a `ref` on each failed call, a call without a recording under `failed` with `recording.missing`, no `without_recording`). The overview (index) is rewritten as a sales page: the reader's gain, the ideas a newcomer would not guess, an example from the bundled sample call log, why pbx against the tools on its comparison page, a start and plain limits. RU/ES index retranslated, changelog and commands updated and accepted, and the changelog link correction moved to v0.8.0. The roadmap did not change.

wordpress.conclusion: Reviewed wordpress 0.3.0 from its changelog and the docs diff since v0.2.0: WireCat Desktop signs in to WordPress in its own window (`--wcat-describe` lists the application-password sign-in with `--site` and `--login`), `posts publish` and `posts unpublish` ask one question, and `--help` names the application password and the `/wp-json` index. The roadmap did not change. RU and ES changelog, commands and permissions updated and accepted.

attio.conclusion: Reviewed attio v0.6.0 to v0.8.0 from its changelog, the docs diff between the tags and the generated command reference. New in 0.8.0: with the `activities` setting on, `sync` copies Attio meetings with the transcripts of their finished call recordings, put on the deals of the people and companies who took part (src/meetings.ts), needing `meeting:read` and `call_recording:read` (scope row in installation), no meetings without `meeting:read`, a call kept up to its first 20,000 characters (usage section "Notes and tasks on a deal", index Limits, roadmap). 0.7.0: built on cli-core 1.0.0 and cli-base 1.0.0, store version 73 that only cli-core 1.0 tools open, `store migrate --no-backup`, `sync --allow-deletions <count>` past the mass-deletion guard (owner only, not over MCP), a kind Attio could not list whole marks nothing deleted, `permission_error` for a refused folder over MCP, the commands contents list names `activities`. RU/ES of index, installation, usage, roadmap, commands and changelog follow the new source. Portal corrections added for index (opening and What you get gain calls), installation (update the other WireCat tools together) and usage (what to do when the guard holds a sync), to move upstream at the next bump. The roadmap is unchanged in Next and Later: one-click sign-in, custom objects and lists, webhooks have not shipped.

hubspot.conclusion: Reviewed hubspot 0.6.0 from its changelog and the docs diff since v0.5.0. Added: `activities create comment|task` and `activities close`, so notes and tasks no longer need `api`. Changed: `account remove` and the second sign-in check are cli-core shared CRM ones, `--delete-data` refuses when another profile account is unknown, and `session start` refuses the profile names `files` and `foreign-contacts`. Fixed: `api notes-create` and `api tasks-create` also check `activities.create`. The roadmap drops the Desktop sign-in item, which shipped in Desktop 0.7.4 (the site correction for it is removed); its remaining item, browser sign-in as yourself, did not ship and stays planned. RU and ES changelog, commands, compare, index, permissions, roadmap and usage updated and accepted.
